subject: Renewal addendum: reserved GPU upsize + on-demand spillover terms

Subject: Renewal addendum: reserved GPU upsize + on-demand spillover terms

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our renewal timeline I attached a draft addendum that does two things we discussed:

- Upsizes your reserved pool from 80 -> 120 GPUs (quarterly committed units) to support the new high-throughput batch jobs.
- Adds an on-demand spillover tier for bursts above the reserved pool. We propose a soft spillover arrangement (rate-limited, pre-warmed nodes where possible) priced at 2.5x the reserved unit rate with a monthly cap option.

I've attached DataWave_Renewal_Addendum_v1.pdf and a throughput_sizing.csv that shows our projections based on your Q4 job mix. High level asks:
1) Can procurement confirm whether a monthly soft-cap (billing cap) is acceptable versus a strict hard cap?
2) If procurement requires a hard cap, what is the guaranteed max monthly spend we should target so we can propose a pricing path and fallback model?

If helpful, I can loop in Laura and Dev for a short technical walkthrough on how the soft spillover will throttle and how failover to model variants is handled.

Next step: if this looks directionally right, we'll produce a redline-ready addendum for legal.

Best,
Ben Carter

Ben —

Thanks for the draft. The upsizing is in line with what we expected, but procurement has specific requirements around any "on-demand" billing. Their ask is simple: for budget forecasting we need an absolute monthly cap per region for billed GPU spend (not just a soft cap). Without a hard cap they won't sign off on auto-renewal.

Two clarifying questions:
- Can Redwood offer a hard cap option (true hard cap that will not bill past X) even if it comes with a larger uplift?
- If not feasible, what guardrails / credits can you offer to make the financial exposure acceptable? For example, a monthly credit if we exceed a threshold, or an overage rate-tier that kicks in after 120% of committed usage.

I've copied our procurement contact to coordinate. We'll need a term sheet we can show legal by EOD Friday.

—Elena
Elena Ramos, Head of AI Ops | DataWave.ai

Subject: Re: Renewal addendum: reserved GPU upsize + on-demand spillover terms

Hi Elena / Procurement team,

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a hard cap option, but it changes the operational and commercial tradeoffs. Two configurations we can propose:

A) Hard-cap plan (no billing over the cap):
- We enforce a strict quota once the cap is reached. Any requests beyond cap receive a 429/Quota exceeded error or are queued.
- Pricing: higher uplift on reserved unit rate (proposed: 1.9x on the reserved unit) to compensate for reservation and opportunity cost.
- Pros: predictable spend. Cons: potential job failures/queueing during unexpected bursts.

B) Soft-spill plan (recommended for critical jobs):
- On-demand spillover that executes spikes above reserved pool. Throttled by policy; pre-warmed ephemeral nodes when available.
- Billing: 2.5x reserved rate, with a configurable monthly protection band (e.g., up to +25% reserved usage billed at 1.5x; beyond that 2.5x) and an optional monthly overage credit if spikes exceed agreed thresholds.
- Pros: keeps pipelines running; avoids failed jobs. Cons: variable spend unless capped.

Operational controls we will include in either plan: per-route SLOs, burst windows, rate-limits, and an automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants if specified. I attached a proposed pricing appendix in the addendum PDF.

Action items:
- Procurement: pick A or B (or ask for a hybrid where mission-critical routes use B and batch jobs use A).
- If A, please provide the target monthly cap number so I can produce an updated addendum with the adjusted uplift.
- If B, tell us acceptable protection band and overage credit thresholds.

Copying Laura and Dev for technical confirmation and to prepare a short note on behavior under cap.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Renewal addendum: reserved GPU upsize + on-demand spillover terms

Hi all,

Quick technical note to help procurement decide:

1) Hard cap behavior (if selected):
- Requests that exceed the cap will receive a 429. For batch jobs we recommend a client-side retry backoff so the queues drain; for streaming/interactive jobs we'd recommend using per-route throttling and graceful degradation (send shorter contexts or lower-cost model variants).
- We can optionally offer a "preemptive throttle" window: when you hit 90% of cap we start shedding non-critical batch jobs to avoid a sudden hard stop.

2) Soft-spill behavior (recommended for critical workloads):
- Spillover is handled by a prioritized queue with a concurrency ceiling. We pre-warm nodes when forecasted load surpasses threshold.
- KV cache and prefix caching remain active across ephemeral nodes to reduce token costs where possible.

3) Billing instrumentation and visibility:
- Per-route telemetry in Redwood Console (token-level, per-model, latency) and daily spike reports.
- We can place an automated alert at 80%, 95%, and 100% of any agreed cap.

4) Implementation timeline and testing:
- If DataWave accepts the design today, we can stand up the expanded reserved pool and a soft-spill pilot in 10 business days, with a 72-hr soak test.

Attached is throughput_sizing.csv with our simulation across your job mix (batch vs interactive).

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk procurement/legal through the failure modes.

—Dev Patel
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ben / Redwood team —

Thanks for the options. Procurement prefers a hybrid approach: mission-critical real-time routes (we'll provide a route list) should be on the soft-spill plan (B) to avoid customer-impacting failures. All large batch ETL jobs should be on the hard-cap plan (A) to keep monthly spend predictable.

A couple of follow-ups:
- We need the exact uplift numbers in the addendum text (you listed 1.9x and 2.5x verbally). Please update the PDF addendum with explicit formulas and a worked example showing billed spend at 90%, 125%, and 150% of committed usage.
- Legal will expect a clause that allows us to set a "billing hard stop" for specified routes in the event of runaway usage after notice.
- We'll send the route list and an initial target hard cap for batch jobs by EOD today.

Attached we will later upload our redlines; for now we need the updated addendum and a DocuSign-ready document by Friday COB.
